resources.string:
OpenWild helps you identify plants and mushrooms from photos, offline.

Photo identification can be wrong. Some deadly species look almost identical to edible ones.

Never eat anything based only on this app. In an emergency, seek medical help.
Show survival value first and highlight deadly species.
Choose a region to start. Nothing is selected until you pick one.
Photo ID is coming soon. Meanwhile, the full offline field guide is ready: tap Explore to search every species.
You seem to be in %1$s. That is only a suggestion — tap it if it is the region you want.
Nothing is selected until you tap a region. A region already saved on this phone works offline. Others download when you tap them, or show as coming soon.
Tip: photograph the whole plant, a leaf up close, and any flower or fruit.
Tip: photograph the cap, the underside (gills or pores), and the stem down to the base. Dig the base out gently.
Camera permission is needed to take photos. You can still choose photos from your gallery.
Could be %1$s — DEADLY. Do not eat.
Add another photo for more confidence
Not confident enough to show eating information. Do not eat.
This doesn\'t match anything in your region pack. Treat as unsafe.
No safety information yet. Treat as unsafe. Do not eat.
For mushrooms, eating information needs at least 2 photos including the underside (gills or pores).
Mushrooms are a poor survival food: very few calories and high risk. Prioritise plants.
Psychoactive. Contains substances controlled in many countries. Possession or use may be illegal where you are. Toxic and deadly lookalikes exist.
Never eat anything based only on this app.
Cooking does NOT make it safe
No survival information in this pack yet.
Couldn\'t reach the pack list. Connect to the internet to download packs.
No internet access. No account. Nothing leaves your phone.
Learn what to never touch or eat
Food, water, fire and shelter plants
I found what might be %1$s (%2$d%% confidence), identified offline with OpenWild. Confirm it on iNaturalist to help science.
Downloaded regions stay on this phone. Updates are offered when a newer pack is published, and nothing downloads until you agree.
Not installed · import its region file
Survival priorities: shelter, water, fire, then food. Never eat anything you can\'t identify with certainty. Plants first; mushrooms last.
Created by EDM producer Zen V
I\'m a US Marine, and we may be foraging for survival one day. This is the go-to app. Hope you enjoy.
Free forever, open source, and private. A gift to anyone who finds themselves in the wild.
OpenWild is free with no ads. If it helped you, you can send a tip over Bitcoin Lightning:
No Lightning wallet found. Address copied to clipboard.
This address is on the clipboard. If your wallet does not fill in the payee, paste it. OpenWild does not send the payment.
No Lightning wallet opened. %1$s is copied — paste it into a wallet.
Found a bug, a wrong ID, or have an idea? Tell us. Nothing is sent until you press send.

OpenWild goes online for one thing only: the public list of region packs on GitHub, and a pack you agree to download. It sends nothing about you. Identification, your notes and your photos stay on the phone, with or without signal. No account, no ads, no analytics, no tracking, no cloud backup. Location never leaves the device. Share, submit and feedback buttons only hand text to another app when you tap them.
Botanists, mycologists and translators: every safety entry is reviewed by people. Share confirmed sightings on iNaturalist to help train future versions.
This safety warning covers its whole genus or family, not this exact species. Treat as unsafe.

While the app is open it checks for a newer pack for the regions you installed, and asks before downloading. Large downloads prefer Wi-Fi and are never started on mobile data unless you agree. The app itself still does not update on its own. For that, install the free, open-source app Obtainium and add the address below, or download the newest OpenWild.apk whenever you like.
%1$s can be updated (%2$s). Download now? The field guide keeps working offline either way. Nothing is downloaded until you tap Download.
%1$s can be updated (%2$s). You are not on Wi-Fi, and this is a large download. Wi-Fi is a better way to get it. Nothing is downloaded unless you agree to use mobile data.
A rating, a review, and your own photos stay on this phone. No account. Nothing is sent unless you tap Submit.
Not medical advice. Never eat a plant you have not identified for yourself.
What you noticed. Not a guide to eating it.
Opens the share sheet so you can email it or send it yourself. OpenWild does not upload anything.
Or open a text-only GitHub issue
